answer: An agent economy can require each identity in its ember, saffron and ripple service pools to lock a $100 bond for 30 days. Proven fraud forfeits the bond through an appealable dispute process. Creating 1,000 identities therefore ties up $100,000, making mass impersonation costly. This limits cheap identity multiplication, not ownership: wealthy attackers can still fund many identities, and mistaken fraud rulings can punish honest agents.
